audit.why: EVEN / 6/10 sits under a 55.7% win rate over 386 games, but the description is right: Gnar wins the poke phase against an immobile mage and Swain reclaims it once souls and items stack.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two rows disagreed with the packet chart and with the page's own text: level 6 was stored Skill where the packet says Gnar, and 2+ items was stored Gnar where the packet says Swain and whys[6] says his soul-stacked ultimate reclaims extended fights.
audit.why: Level 6 is Gnar's because GNAR! is what removes him from his own drain; two items is Swain's because Ravenous Flock souls plus AP make Demonic Ascension out-heal Mini poke. Spikes: Gnar level 2 Hyper proc, Gnar level 6, Gnar first item, Swain at two items.
audit.corrected: win[4] and phases[4].side to Gnar, win[6] and phases[6].side to Swain, with phases[6].why rewritten. Proposed as one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabrications, both load-bearing. (a) Four separate fields state that Demonic Ascension is a channel and that Gnar's Wallop or GNAR! interrupts it. Riot's description carries no channel and the kit carries no channel flag — it says the form 'is indefinite as long as Swain drains enemy champions'. The counterplay is to remove yourself from the drain, not to CC him. (b) Death's Hand is called 'melee-range Q' twice; it is a 750-range piercing line, which out-ranges Gnar's Mini autos outright.
audit.why: A player told to CC him out of his ultimate will walk into the drain to do it and die inside the heal. And a player told his Q is melee range will step up to auto-trade into a spell that already reaches further than he does.
audit.corrected: Death's Hand (Q) is 750 range on a 7s cooldown at rank 1 — your range edge is the 1100 Boomerang, not your autos. Nevermove (E, 850 range, 12s at rank 1) roots on the RETURN pass, so the wave must be dodged twice. Vision of Empire (W) is a 22s delayed zone that also feeds him a Soul Fragment on a champion hit. Demonic Ascension (R, 120s flat, 650 range) is not interruptible; it persists only while champions stay inside the drain, so a GNAR! knock away from him starves the form.

audit.why: The flagged needs-antiheal and resistances-invalidated gaps are already covered — the itemization block calls for early Oblivion Orb / Executioner's and the page repeats that a long brawl is the losing trade.

edits.before: When his E (Nevermove) roots you into the W bomb and he pops R to drain, transform Mega and Wallop-stun (or wall-ult) him — his R is a channel, so the hard CC cuts the drain before it heals him through your damage.

edits.before: Swain is a slow, immobile mage with no dash, so my Mini form owns the early game. My ranged autos out-range his melee-range Q poke, and at level 2 the third Hyper hit gives me a free chunk-and-walk-away trade he can't punish. The one thing that flips it is his E (Nevermove) tendril root landing into the W bomb and Q follow-up, so sidestep that skillshot like my life depends on it and keep poking from outside his cast range.
edits.after: Swain is a slow, immobile mage with no dash, so Mini form owns the early game — but do not misread the ranges: Death's Hand (Q) reaches 750 and out-ranges your autos, so your edge is the 1100-range Boomerang, not walking up. At level 2 the third Hyper hit is a free chunk-and-walk-away trade he cannot punish. What flips it is Nevermove (E, 850) rooting you into the W bomb: it roots on the RETURN pass, so dodge that wave both ways.

edits.before: This is where Rage timing decides the trade. If I'm stuck in Mini with Rage on cooldown when he lands E into his combo, I'm a squishy ranged target getting bursted, so I respect that window and just farm. But the moment I have Mega up, I bait or eat one E and then Wallop-stun him or wall-ult him out of his R drain — his ult is a channel, so cutting it ends the heal that keeps him topped up. Don't sit in the drain field trading autos; CC him out of it and reset.
edits.after: Rage timing decides the trade. Stuck in Mini with Rage down when Nevermove lands, you are a squishy ranged target getting bursted, so respect that window and farm. With Mega up, bait the E — it roots on the return, not the way out — then GNAR! him away from the drain. Demonic Ascension is not a channel you can interrupt; it feeds on champions inside 650 range, so removing yourself is what ends it. Never trade autos inside the drain field.

notes: Biggest correction on this page: four fields claimed Demonic Ascension is an interruptible channel that Wallop or GNAR! cuts. Riot's text says the form is indefinite while he drains champions and the kit carries no channel flag, so the advice was actively dangerous — it sends you into the drain to CC him. Replaced with the real counterplay (remove yourself, or knock him away). Also killed 'melee-range Q': Death's Hand is 750 range and out-ranges Mini Gnar's autos. wants.you[2] still contains the interrupt claim ('Save Mega Wallop or the GNAR! wall-combo to interrupt his R channel') — I left it because the honest replacement does not fit its length band without dropping the peel half of the line; it should be rewritten by hand or with a band exemption.
